findings.title: enableSqlExpressions contains inverted, dead feature-flag logic that invites accidental re-enabling
findings.body: The new helper `enableSqlExpressions` reads `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` and then returns `false` in both branches, so the function always returns false regardless of the flag. Besides being dead code, the logic is inverted relative to its name (when the flag is ON, `enabled` is false; when the flag is OFF, `enabled` is true), and the result is never used. A future maintainer 'fixing' the seemingly-wrong inversion (e.g. changing the first branch to `return true`) would silently re-enable the SQL expression code path that this PR deliberately disables for CVE-2024-9264. Since the intent is to unconditionally reject SQL expressions, the flag lookup and helper should be removed entirely and the case body should just return an error directly, making the security intent explicit and unambiguous.

findings.title: Error message "sqlExpressions is not implemented" misleads users about why the query was rejected
findings.body: When a user submits a SQL expression query, they now get `"sqlExpressions is not implemented"`. The feature is implemented but intentionally disabled for security reasons; additionally, the message references the internal feature-toggle name (`sqlExpressions`) which still exists in featuremgmt and can be enabled by admins, yet enabling it has no effect. An admin who enables the `sqlExpressions` feature toggle per the existing documented behavior will still get this error with no indication that the flag is now a no-op. The message should state that SQL expressions are disabled/unavailable (and ideally the flag should be removed or documented as non-functional).

findings.title: No tests verify that SQL expression queries are rejected, and existing SQL tests are not updated
findings.body: This PR changes the behavior of the SQL expression query type from executing (behind the `sqlExpressions` feature flag) to always failing, but adds no test asserting the new behavior (e.g. that ReadQuery with QueryTypeSQL returns an error, and that the go-duck-backed TablesList/QueryFramesInto paths are never reachable). Existing tests covering SQL expressions in pkg/expr (e.g. tests constructing SQLCommand or calling sql.TablesList) would now fail against the 'not implemented' stubs if they exercise the removed functionality, and no updated tests are included in the changed files. A regression test is needed so that a future refactor cannot silently re-enable this path without a test failure.

findings.title: Stub DB methods keep unreachable code paths in SQLCommand.Execute alive with silent failure semantics
findings.body: The new `DB` stub makes every method return `errors.New("not implemented")`. Because `NewSQLCommand` calls `sql.TablesList` (which now always fails) the command can never be constructed, so `SQLCommand.Execute` is dead code — yet it still contains a live call to `db.QueryFramesInto` whose error is swallowed into `rsp.Error` and returned as a successful (nil-error) result. If the construction-time guard is ever relaxed (e.g. by re-enabling the flag), queries would fail at execute time with a generic 'not implemented' error surfaced as query data rather than a clear server-side rejection. Consider deleting or clearly deprecating the unreachable Execute body, or failing fast, so the disabled state is enforced in one place only.
